newsitem.title: FRANCE: Economic climate unsatisfactory - Club Med.
newsitem.headline: Economic climate unsatisfactory - Club Med.

text.p: Club Mediterranee's target of a 400 million franc profit for 1996/97 had assumed a more favourable economic climate, director Antoine Cachin said.
"(Chairman) Serge Trigano bet on attaining a 400 million profit in 1997 if economic conditions allowed. Apparently the economic climate isn't what we expected," he said.
Cachin declined to say whether the profit target set by Trigano had changed. He also declined to make any forecast for the current year ending on October 31 or 1996/97.
"I don't know what the economic conditions will be in 1997. Today they don't seem satisfactory," he said.

The share was down 18 percent on the bourse at 1300 GMT after Club Med said on Tuesday evening that it expected flat pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit for the second half because vacation-goers were favouring its less expensive packages.
Its pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit was 25 million francs for the second half of 1994/95.

Analysts say the weak spending climate in France, reflecting concerns about the high jobless rate, has cut into spending for leisure activities. Many analysts slashed earnings forecasts for the group and lowered their ratings on the stock.
